metadata.scenario_context: James, Amy, and Lucas, who are colleagues at a technology startup, have recently been given the task to organize a company event to celebrate their startup's success in releasing their first app. The team has been buzzing about a recently published article claiming that the government is planning to lower corporate taxes which will greatly benefit their startup. They decide to discuss the details of the event

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Guatemala have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest a vegetarian-friendly place for the celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss where to host the celebratory event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Hey James, have you thought about where we should hold the celebration? I was thinking we could find a nice vegetarian-friendly place? It could cater to everyone's dietary preferences. 

Also, about that article regarding the government lowering corporate taxes — do you really think we can trust the press on that? I mean, they always seem to have their own agendas. What’s your take?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: A vegetarian-friendly place sounds good... I guess we need to consider something that fits our budget too. But about the press... I honestly don't have any confidence in what they say. In Guatemala, we’ve learned to question everything the media reports. It’s hard to trust them when they always seem to have their own agendas... I just wouldn’t take that article at face value.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
I get that budget is important, but we can definitely find a place that's both vegetarian-friendly and budget-conscious. 

As for the press, I mean, in the U.S., we typically have a lot of confidence in what they report. It seems to be a bit different here. But I think that article could hold some weight, especially if it means more resources for us. So, let’s keep our options open. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: Yeah, I’m sure we can find something that fits both criteria. But I still really struggle to trust the press. It’s just... I’ve seen too many inconsistencies and misleading information. I think we should focus on what we can control rather than rely on what they say. It’s better to be cautious. Let’s prioritize the event location for now.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:

But I still believe, generally, that we can trust what the press puts out. I mean, it’s important to stay informed about developments that could benefit us. Anyway, let's focus on the location first. Do you have any places in mind?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: I agree that it’s important to include everyone. For locations, I was thinking maybe we could check out that new vegetarian café downtown? I've heard good things about it. But back to the press... I just can’t shake the feeling that we should be skeptical. We need to gather our own information instead of relying on what they say. Let’s see what options we have for the café then.

The new vegetarian café downtown sounds like a great idea! I’ve heard good things too, and it could be a fun place for the celebration. 

Regarding the press, I understand your skepticism. But I still feel like there’s a lot of reliable information out there if we look for it. It just helps to stay connected to what's happening around us. Anyway, let’s focus on checking out the café. When do you think we should visit it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: I think the café is a solid choice, and I agree we should check it out soon. But honestly, I don't really see meaningful differences here when it comes to trusting the press. At the end of the day, it’s all the same. Live and let live, right? I’m sure people figure it out as we go along. Let's just focus on picking a date to visit the café. How about this weekend?

But I just want to say that I genuinely believe that we shouldn’t dismiss the press entirely. There are definitely trustworthy sources out there that provide valuable insights. Still, I can respect your perspective on living and letting live. So, shall we set a time to meet at the café this weekend?
